PhD thesis, Ball State University (ix + 223 leaves; advisor Herbert Stahlke); author's abstract on the Ball State Cardinal Scholar record hdl:20.500.14291/174922 (published version: Baloubi, Desire 2005, same title, Charlotte NC: Conquering Books). Corroboration: Kluge, Angela (2011). A sociolinguistic survey of the Ede language communities of Benin and Togo, Volume 4: Idaca language area. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2011-005, 39 pp.
catalog_locator: Baloubi 2000: dc.description.abstract of the Cardinal Scholar record (https://cardinalscholar.bsu.edu/handle/20.500.14291/174922; thesis body not deposited). Kluge 2011 vol. 4: sec. 5.1.1 'Internal comprehension', p. 12 (PDF p. 17), repeated in the summary p. 21 (PDF p. 26).
catalog_quote: [Baloubi 2000, author's abstract:] Particular attention is paid to vowel harmony (VH) and tones. ... In regard to tones, it is pointed out that a three-way tonal system is a major characteristic of the language. However, a phenomenon of M/L neutralization is underlined in a specific environment: a final low tone in a verb followed by a direct object noun. In this environment, a low (L) tone changes to mid (M) ... like Standard Yoruba (SY), Idaacha has open syllables: V and CV. [Kluge 2011 vol. 4, p. 12:] Linguistic differences between the different Idaca villages throughout the area are reportedly minor and mainly phonological or at the level of tone

new_statements.citation: Kluge, Angela (2011). A sociolinguistic survey of the Ede language communities of Benin and Togo, Introduction and Volume 1: Ede language family - Background and assessment methodology. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2011-002, xi + 209 pp; and Volume 4: Idaca language area, SIL ESR 2011-005, 39 pp.
new_statements.check: reported by the second reader, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Not a stress statement, but for the record: Kluge 2011 Vol 4 (Idaca language area, SIL ESR 2011-005), PDF p. 17 (sec. 5.1.1 Internal comprehension) and p. 26 (summary): 'Linguistic differences between the different Idaca villages throughout the area are reportedly minor and mainly phonological or at the level of tone, without bringing about a semantic change.' This presupposes Idaca is tonal (consistent with Baloubi's three-way system) but says nothing about stress. Intro+Vol 1, Appendix K note 36 (PDF p. 93): 'Tone markings were transcribed but were not included in the analysis due to ambiguities in proper weighting.' No stress content in either volume.
